title: A spectroscopic method for monitoring photochemical reactions in the gas phase
author: Behera, Das

steps.title: Modify and Align Gas Cell
steps.instruction: Replace the borosilicate glass body of the gas cell with a quartz tube (diameter 11 cm, length 19 cm, thickness 2 mm). Install the three gold‑coated concave mirrors (two adjustable at the top, one fixed at the bottom) according to the white‑cell principle. Set the infrared optical path length to 7.2 m by moving the adjustable mirror and counting He‑Ne laser spots on the fixed mirror (1 spot = 0.8 m).

steps.title: Assemble Vacuum Line
steps.instruction: Build a homemade vacuum line from 1/4" Swagelok valves, tubing and fittings. Connect it to the gas cell, a pressure transducer (PRM‑300 MX, IRA), a vacuum pump (RV8, Boc Edward), an Ultra‑Torr fitting for the sample tube or bulb, and an argon reservoir cylinder. Use a fluorocarbon (FKM) O‑ring on the Ultra‑Torr fitting. Argon serves both for cleaning the cell and as the carrier gas.

steps.title: Configure UV Photolysis Optics
steps.instruction: Generate 266 nm light from the fourth harmonic of a 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser (PRO‑230, Spectra Physics). Separate the fundamental and harmonic beams with a Pellin‑Broca prism placed near the laser head. Construct a multi‑pass UV arrangement using five UV reflectors mounted on circular holders attached to a rectangular frame that allows x‑ and y‑adjustments. Align the reflector set parallel to the gas‑cell body so that the UV beam makes six passes through the cell, covering an irradiation volume of approximately 20.3 cm³. Measure the laser pulse energy before it enters the cell (37 ± 3 mJ per pulse).

steps.title: Load Sample and Prepare Gas Mixture
steps.instruction: Load the sample (e.g., chlorobenzene, C6H5Cl) into a glass tube or bulb appropriate for its state and attach it to the vacuum line via the Ultra‑Torr fitting. Remove dissolved gases by performing several freeze‑pump‑thaw cycles. Expand the sample vapor at 298 K into the vacuum line, then transfer it to the gas cell and mix with ~140 Torr of ultra‑high‑purity argon (UHP). Adjust the amount of precursor so that its infrared absorbance stays below 1.2 (typically <0.5 Torr of sample vapor). Determine the partial pressure inside the cell from the integrated infrared absorbance. Continuously purge the spectrometer sample compartment with UHP nitrogen to avoid moisture and CO₂ interference.

steps.title: Acquire Baseline and Photolysis Spectra
steps.instruction: Record the infrared spectrum of the precursor without photolysis at a spectral resolution of 2 cm⁻¹, averaging 128 scans (≈53 s). Verify precursor stability by measuring spectra at several minute‑intervals. Start the UV laser irradiation and, simultaneously, begin infrared data acquisition. Use the FT‑IR repeated‑mode to acquire five spectra at 120 s intervals, for a total acquisition time of about 9 min. Each individual scan requires 414 ms at 2 cm⁻¹ resolution over the 4000–700 cm⁻¹ region.

steps.title: Process Data to Obtain Difference Spectra
steps.instruction: Manually trigger the laser irradiation and the repetitive FT‑IR scan measurement at the same time. Subtract the precursor spectrum (with appropriate weighting) from each spectrum recorded during photolysis to generate difference spectra. Identify depletion of reactant bands and appearance of product bands in the difference spectra. Process all data with OPUS software (version 7.2, Bruker Optics) and perform baseline correction and quantitative absorbance analysis with GRAMS/AI (version 7.02, Thermo Galactic).
